title: Edom's Ultimate Downfall: A Prophecy
paragraphs: So, here's the deal with Edom — this is Obadiah's message, straight from God. A messenger went to the nations that don't follow God with this message:
'Get up and get ready to fight Edom!'

God's telling Edom, 'Listen, I'm about to make you irrelevant, the most looked-down-on nation. You think you're all that, living up in the mountains, thinking no one can touch you. But you're wrong. Even if you hung out on a high cliff like an eagle, even if you built your nest in the stars, I'd bring you down.' And that's a promise from God.

'If thieves came, they'd take everything, right? Well, Esau's going to be completely wrecked. Your allies will turn on you, your friends will betray you, and your world will fall apart. You won't see it coming. So don't be shocked—this is God's sure word—when I get rid of all the wise and powerful people in Edom. Your heroes will abandon you, Teman, and no one will be left in your mountains. This is all because of how you treated your brother, Jacob. You'll be disgraced and forgotten. When foreigners attacked Jerusalem and took your brother's people, you just stood there and watched. You were just as bad as them. You shouldn't have celebrated their suffering or taken advantage of them when they were at their lowest. You shouldn't have blocked their escape or handed over the survivors.'

'God's day of judgment is coming for all nations. What you've done will be done to you. It's coming back to hit you. Just like you partied on my holy mountain, all the other nations will drink God's anger. They'll drink and drink and drink—they'll drink themselves to death. But on Mount Zion, there will be safety. Jacob's family will get back everything that was taken from them. Jacob's family will catch fire, Joseph's family will become a fierce flame, and Esau's family will be like straw, completely burned up—nothing left but a pile of ashes.' God has spoken.

Then, people from the south will take over Edom's mountains, and people from the foothills will take over the Philistine's land. They'll reclaim the lands of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will take Gilead. The exiled Israelites will return and take over the land of Canaan, all the way to Zarephath. And the Jerusalem exiles from the far northwest in Sepharad will come back and take over the cities in the south. The survivors on Mount Zion will go into the mountains of Esau and rule justly and fairly—a kingdom that honors God.
